subject: Embedding units, dimensions, and bulk pricing — DataAurora rate request
messages:
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@dataaurora.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@dataaurora.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Embedding rate info and packaging questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking a look at our RFP. We're evaluating embeddings for a large-scale semantic search project and want to understand Redwood's hosted pricing and packaging assumptions before we proceed with a pilot. A few specific asks:

- How do you bill embeddings today — per-vector, per-token, or both? If per-vector, is there a distinction by dimension (e.g., 512 vs 1536 vs 4096)?
- What are typical unit sizes (vector = 1 embedding) and how do you treat indexable documents that produce multiple embeddings?
- Do you have published bulk thresholds / committed volume discounts (e.g., 10M, 100M vectors)? Example pricing tiers would be great.
- Which models are supported for embeddings in the hosted API and are there price differences by model family?
- Any practical guidance on how to estimate monthly cost for ~50M short text embeddings (average length ~5 tokens) versus 10M long-form (avg ~200 tokens) — do we mix token and vector billing?

I've attached the RFP and a sample usage CSV to illustrate our distribution. We need a baseline estimate and an outline of minimum deal/commit terms to budget for a pilot next quarter.

Appreciate any high-level numbers you can share.

Best,
Hannah Lee
Head of Data Platforms
DataAurora

--
Attachment: DataAurora_RFP_2027.pdf (application/pdf)
Attachment: sample-embed-usage.csv (text/csv)
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@dataaurora.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Embedding rate info and packaging questions

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the RFP and the sample. Quick answers up front, then Ben (copied) will follow up with a simple rate card and options for commitments:

1) Billing model: Hosted embeddings are billed per-vector by default for most customers. For very long inputs we also surface a token-based estimate to help estimate costs, but our backend normalizes to vectors for invoicing.

2) Dimensions: We support multiple output dimensions (512, 1024, 1536, 4096). Pricing is generally per-vector and varies by dimension class — higher-dim vectors carry a higher unit price. We don't split billing by individual token counts when vectors are used for indexing; tokens matter more for generation endpoints.

3) Bulk / commitment discounts: We do publish tiered discounts for volume; typical starting points: 0–1M, 1M–10M, 10M–100M, 100M+. Deeper discounts are available with committed monthly or annual spends. Ben will propose a few concrete tier examples and an estimated monthly cost for your shape of usage.

4) Supported models: Hosted embeddings currently include Redwood-Embed-small (512), Redwood-Embed-medium (1536), and two partner families (OpenEmbed-1536, OpenEmbed-4096). Model-specific pricing varies — partner models may have a premium. We can also host custom fine-tuned embed models under Dedicated or Private agreements.

5) Estimation guidance: For a mix like you described, we usually convert long-form into multiple vectors (e.g., 200-token doc -> 3–4 vectors depending on chunking). In your CSV I see distribution that suggests ~65M vectors total for the combined workloads; I'll ask Ben to show a cost table for 50M and 100M vector commitments and a no-commit baseline.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week to walk through the CSV and align on chunking assumptions.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@dataaurora.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Embedding rate info and packaging questions

Hannah —

Thanks for the details. Per Mina's note, attached below is a concise baseline rate card and two sample commitment scenarios. High level:

- No-commit (on-demand hosted): 0–1M vectors $0.00045/vector (512-d), 0.00065/vector (1536-d), 0.0020/vector (4096-d)
- Mid-commit (12 mo, 10M/mo): 10% discount off on-demand unit rate
- Large-commit (12 mo, 50M/mo): 25% discount off on-demand unit rate + SLA uplift

Example monthly math (approx):
- 50M short-text vectors (512-d) on no-commit = 50,000,000 * $0.00045 = $22,500/mo
- 10M long-form vectors (1536-d) on mid-commit pricing = 10,000,000 * ($0.00065 * 0.90) = $5,850/mo

Notes and clarifications:
- We round up partially produced vectors per chunking policy; we'll confirm the exact chunking params after review of your sample.
- If you need a token-based fallback for a small % of calls we can include hybrid billing but invoices reflect vectors once indexable embeddings are created.
- Model premiums: partner-hosted 4096-d models carry ~3–4x the base 512-d price due to compute.

Marissa — can you confirm whether DataAurora's procurement would require a minimum annual commitment/PO for mid-commit offer? Also dropping a link to the draft MS/SA for quick review.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Embedding rate info and packaging questions

Thanks Ben/Mina — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying items from procurement and engineering after reviewing your numbers:

- Procurement: mid-commit sounds reasonable but we need clarity on invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether unused committed vectors roll over.
- Engineering: can you confirm the exact chunking heuristic you used to estimate 50M -> 65M vectors? We want to validate the chunk size and overlap assumptions (e.g., 256-token windows with 32-token overlap).

If you can confirm rollover policy and chunking parameters, procurement will prepare a preliminary PO for the mid-commit tier (10M/mo) and we can plan a pilot kickoff. Also, does the mid-commit include discounted model premiums or are those outside the commitment discount?

Can we aim to finalize terms next week? Happy to schedule a 30-min call if that helps.

Best,
Hannah
Head of Data Platforms
DataAurora
